chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran
chunks.text:
The defaults that make the same source give different numbers, or fail differently, under each compiler. Every
row was measured on small programs (gfortran 16, ifx 2025.3, nvfortran 26.1, x86-64 Linux with FMA); the
compiler documents of this pack give the details.

chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran > Defaults that change results
chunks.text:
| | gfortran | ifx | nvfortran |
|---|---|---|---|
| optimisation without `-O` | 0 | 2 (0 with `-g`) | 1 (0 with `-g`) |
| FMA contraction by default | only when the target has FMA (`-march=...`), not at `-O0` | only with an FMA target (`-xHost`, `-march=...`) | yes, at every level (host target) |
| turn contraction off | `-ffp-contract=off` | `-no-fma` or `-fp-model precise` | `-Mnofma` |
| value-unsafe optimisation by default | no | yes (`-fp-model fast=1`) | no |
| Kahan sum kept at `-O2` | yes | no (needs `-fp-model precise`) | yes |
| NaN tests broken by | `-ffast-math`, `-ffinite-math-only` | `-fp-model fast=2` | not observed (`-fast` kept them) |

Consequence: a result that differs between compilers in the last digits is not, by itself, a bug. To find
where the difference comes from, rebuild with contraction off and value-safe models on every compiler
(`-ffp-contract=off`; `-fp-model precise`; `-Mnofma`): if the results then agree within rounding, the
difference was FMA or reassociation. `fobis assess` measures this spread for a declared case with its
`compiler` and `rounding` families.

chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran > Defaults that change failures
chunks.text:
| | gfortran | ifx | nvfortran |
|---|---|---|---|
| automatic arrays and temporaries | heap (stack with `-fstack-arrays`, part of `-Ofast`) | stack (`-heap-arrays` moves them) | heap in the measured cases |
| uninitialised real with checks | SIGFPE (`-finit-real=snan -ffpe-trap=invalid`) | located (`-init=snan,arrays -fpe0`) | quiet NaN, no trap (`-Minit-real=snan`) |
| bounds error message | `At line N of file F` | `forrtl: severe (408)` + traceback table | `Subscript out of range for array a (F: N)` |
| sanitizer | `-fsanitize=address,undefined` | `-fsanitize=address` (ifort: ignored) | none |

`fobis build --shadow checks` and `--shadow sanitize` apply the right flags per compiler; `fobis matrix` runs a
project's tests and cases under several compilers and shadows.

chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran > Promotion flags promote different declarations
chunks.text:
| Flags | real | double precision | real(real32) | real(real64) |
|-------|------|------------------|--------------|--------------|
| gfortran `-fdefault-real-8` | 8 | 16 | 4 | 8 |
| gfortran `-freal-4-real-8` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| ifx `-real-size 64` | 8 | 8 | 4 | 8 |
| nvfortran `-r8` | 8 | 8 | 4 | 8 |

Only gfortran's `-freal-4-real-8` promotes explicit kinds. A code with a kind module (`R8P`, `real64`) is promoted
portably by changing the kind parameter, not by flags.

chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran > Module files and libraries
chunks.text:
`.mod` files are compiler-specific: ifx (`error #7013`) and nvfortran (`NVFORTRAN-F-0004-Corrupt or Old
Module file`) refuse gfortran's, and old gfortran releases refuse the format of new ones. Every library used
through modules (MPI, HDF5, NetCDF, a fetched FoBiS dependency built as a library) must be built by the same
compiler, in a module format it reads. With `use=sources` dependencies FoBiS compiles them with the project's
compiler, which avoids the problem.

chunks.heading: Comparing gfortran, ifx and nvfortran > Symbol names in linker errors
chunks.text:
Module procedures get different link names: `__m_MOD_p` (gfortran), `m_mp_p_` (ifx, ifort), `m_p_` (nvfortran)
for procedure `p` of module `m`. An undefined reference to a name of another compiler's form means objects or
libraries built by a different compiler are being linked: rebuild everything with one compiler
(`fobis build --force-compile`). `fobis build --explain` recognises these names and reports the procedure and
module.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran)
GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Default optimisation and debug information
chunks.text:
Without an `-O` flag gfortran compiles at `-O0`; `-O` alone means `-O1`; the last `-O` on the command line wins.
`-g` adds debug information and does not change the optimisation level. An optimised build with `-g` still
reorders and inlines code: its backtraces and line numbers can point at the wrong statement. Locate a crash with
an unoptimised build (`-O0 -g`), which is what `fobis build --shadow checks` builds.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Runtime checks
chunks.text:
`-fcheck=all` enables every runtime check: `bounds` (array subscripts, and character lengths of dummy
arguments), `pointer` (pointers and allocatables),
`mem` (allocation failures), `do` (changes to a DO variable inside the loop), `recursion`, `bits` and
`array-temps` (a run-time warning when an array temporary is created). A bounds error is reported with its
location (measured, gfortran 16, `-O0 -g -fcheck=all`):

```
At line 18 of file kernels.f90
Fortran runtime error: Index '11' of dimension 1 of array 'a' above upper bound of 10
```

`-fbacktrace` (on by default) prints a backtrace on runtime errors; frames show `???` without debug information.
Bounds checks cannot check the last dimension of an assumed-size dummy (`a(*)`): it has no upper bound. The
address sanitizer (below) catches an overflow through it.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Floating-point traps and uninitialised reals
chunks.text:
`-ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow` turns invalid operations, division by zero and overflow into `SIGFPE`; the
program stops at the offending operation instead of carrying NaN or Inf. `-finit-real=snan` initialises local
reals to a signalling NaN, so with the `invalid` trap the first arithmetic use of an uninitialised real stops
the program (measured: SIGFPE). Other initialisers: `-finit-integer=N`, `-finit-logical=true`,
`-finit-derived` (components of derived types).

The SIGFPE report is a backtrace; with `-g` it names the line (measured):

```
Program received signal SIGFPE: Floating-point exception - erroneous arithmetic operation.
...
#3  0x6061c8416278 in fpe
	at fpe.f90:5
```

The traps are set for the whole process when the main program starts: code from other libraries running in the
same process traps too, including code that produces an Inf or NaN on purpose.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Sanitizers
chunks.text:
`-fsanitize=address` (AddressSanitizer) finds stack and heap buffer overflows, including a heap overflow
through an assumed-size dummy that `-fcheck=bounds` cannot see (measured), and use after free. LeakSanitizer,
part of it on Linux, reports allocations never freed at exit. `-fsanitize=undefined` adds undefined-behaviour
checks. Both flags must be given to the link as well; keep `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` and `-g` for readable
reports. `fobis build --shadow sanitize` builds with `-O1 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer
-fsanitize=address,undefined`.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Floating-point contraction (FMA)
chunks.text:
gfortran contracts `a*b + c` into a fused multiply-add when the target instruction set has FMA: the default is
`-ffp-contract=fast`. The plain x86-64 target has no FMA, so `-O2` alone gives no contraction; `-march=native`
on an FMA processor, `-march=x86-64-v3` or `-mfma` do. Measured: `a*b + c` with `a*b = 1 - 2**-60` and
`c = -1` gives 0 without FMA and `-2**-60` with it at `-O2`; no contraction at `-O0`; `-ffp-contract=off`
disables it. A change of the `-march=` target alone can therefore change results in the last bits: compare runs built for
the same target, or declare a tolerance.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Fast math
chunks.text:
`-ffast-math` (also part of `-Ofast`) lets the compiler reassociate, assume no NaN or Inf
(`-ffinite-math-only`) and ignore signed zeros. Measured consequences:

- Compensated (Kahan) summation is simplified away: a single-precision Kahan sum of 10^7 terms 0.1 had a relative
  error of 1.5e-8 at `-O2` and 8.8e-2 with `-O2 -ffast-math` (2.4e-2 with `-Ofast`).
- `ieee_is_nan(x)` and `x /= x` return false for a NaN `x` with `-ffast-math` or `-ffinite-math-only`: NaN
  guards silently stop working.

`-O3 -march=native` alone kept IEEE semantics in the same measurement (Kahan sum unchanged).

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Precision promotion flags
chunks.text:
Measured `kind()` of each declaration:

| Flags | real | double precision | real(real32) | real(real64) | real(8) |
|-------|------|------------------|--------------|--------------|---------|
| none | 4 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-fdefault-real-8` | 8 | 16 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-fdefault-real-8 -fdefault-double-8` | 8 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-freal-4-real-8` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| `-freal-4-real-8 -freal-8-real-16` | 8 | 16 | 8 | 16 | 16 |

`-fdefault-real-8` promotes only declarations without a kind (and `double precision` to 16 unless
`-fdefault-double-8`); `-freal-4-real-8` promotes every kind-4 real, explicit kinds included. Promotion changes
record lengths of unformatted files, `storage_size` results and C interoperability: code that stores a real
into an integer of fixed size, or reads binary files written by an unpromoted build, breaks.
`-fdefault-integer-8` makes default integers 8 bytes (measured), which breaks calls into libraries compiled with
4-byte integers (MPI, BLAS) unless they were built the same way. `fobis assess` uses
`-freal-4-real-8 -freal-8-real-16` for its `precision` family with gfortran.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Automatic arrays and the stack
chunks.text:
gfortran allocates large automatic arrays and array temporaries on the heap unless `-fstack-arrays` is given;
`-Ofast` enables `-fstack-arrays`. Measured: an automatic array of 4 million double-precision values (32 MB)
in a subroutine runs at `-O2` and dies with SIGSEGV at `-Ofast` or `-O2 -fstack-arrays` under an 8 MB stack
limit (`ulimit -s 8192`). Raise the limit, or keep large work arrays allocatable. With OpenMP each thread other
than the initial one has a stack sized by `OMP_STACKSIZE`.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Module files
chunks.text:
`.mod` files carry a format version: gfortran 11 to 14 write version 15, gfortran 15 and 16 write version 16
(measured). gfortran 15 and 16 read both versions; gfortran 14 and older refuse version 16 with:

```
Fatal Error: Cannot read module file 'm.mod' opened at (1), because it was created by a different version of GNU Fortran
```

The same rule applies to the `.mod` files of installed libraries (`mpi`, `mpi_f08`, `hdf5`): they must come
from a gfortran that writes a format the compiler reads. After changing compiler, rebuild the project from
scratch (`fobis build --force-compile`): FoBiS's timestamp check does not notice a new compiler with the same
command name. The verification commands (`case`, `verify`, `assess`, `diff-run`, `bench`) rebuild
automatically when the compiler's path or `--version` changes.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Optimisation reports
chunks.text:
`-fopt-info-vec-optimized` and `-fopt-info-vec-missed` report which loops were vectorised and why others were
not, as `file:line:column: optimized: ...` and `missed: ...` lines. `fobis bench --feedback` compares these
reports between two revisions; `fobis lint --compiler-feedback LOG` attributes them to procedures.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Profiling
chunks.text:
`-pg` instruments for gprof: the program writes `gmon.out` at exit (one file per process with
`GMON_OUT_PREFIX`). Compile and link with `-pg`. `fobis profile --tool gprof` builds this variant and maps the
flat profile to the project's procedures.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Standard conformance
chunks.text:
`-std=f2018` (or `f2008`, `f2023`) rejects extensions such as `real*8`; `-pedantic` reports more; `-Werror`
turns warnings into errors. `-Wall -Wextra` warn about unused variables, character truncation and more;
`-Wconversion` about implicit conversions. `fobis build --shadow strict` builds with
`-std=f2018 -pedantic -Werror`.

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Parallel models
chunks.text:
`-fopenmp` enables OpenMP (and links its runtime); `-fopenacc` enables OpenACC, which offloads only with a
gfortran built with an offload target (otherwise the regions run on the host). `-fcoarray=single` compiles
coarray code for one image; `-fcoarray=lib` with the OpenCoarrays library runs several images
(`compiler = opencoarrays-gnu` in a fobos mode uses the `caf` wrapper).

chunks.heading: GNU Fortran (gfortran) > Known bug: EFAULT with pointer sections at -O2
chunks.text:
A pointer array section passed to a dummy declared with an explicit lower bound has produced wrong addresses
(EFAULT, "Bad address") in gfortran at `-O2` and above; documented with a reproducer in the hpc-practice pack,
which `fobis run --explain` cites when it recognises the error.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort)
chunks.text:
Facts about the Intel Fortran compilers that change what a program computes, how it fails, or whether it
builds. "Measured" means observed on small programs with ifx 2025.3 (and ifort 2024.2 where named) on x86-64
Linux with an AVX2/FMA processor. FoBiS uses this family for `compiler = intel_nextgen` (ifx) and
`compiler = intel` (ifort).

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > ifx and ifort
chunks.text:
ifx is the LLVM-based compiler; ifort is the classic one. On the measured installation ifort exists only in the
2024.2 release directory and the 2025.3 release ships ifx alone. New builds should use ifx; the two accept
mostly the same flags but differ in sanitizer support (below) and in some defaults.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Default optimisation and debug information
chunks.text:
Without an `-O` flag ifx optimises at `-O2`; with `-g` and no `-O` it compiles at `-O0` (measured from the
driver's `-###` output). An `-O2` build is the default, so a crash in a build without explicit flags comes from
optimised code: its traceback can name the wrong line. Locate it with `-O0 -g -traceback`, which is what
`fobis build --shadow checks` builds.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Runtime checks
chunks.text:
`-check all` enables bounds, pointer, shape and other runtime checks; `-traceback` prints the call stack with
routine, line and file. A bounds error (measured, `-O0 -g -check all -traceback`):

```
forrtl: severe (408): fort: (2): Subscript #1 of the array A has value 11 which is greater than the upper bound of 10

Image              PC                Routine            Line        Source
bounds             000000000040594F  smooth                     18  kernels.f90
bounds             00000000004052F4  bounds                      6  bounds.f90
```

`-fpe0` traps invalid operations, division by zero and overflow (`forrtl: error (73): floating divide by zero`
with the traceback row of the operation, measured). `-init=snan,arrays` initialises local reals, including
arrays, to a signalling NaN: with `-fpe0` the first use of an uninitialised real stops the program at its line
(measured).

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Floating-point model: fast by default
chunks.text:
ifx's default floating-point model is `-fp-model fast=1`: the compiler may reassociate and simplify
expressions. Measured consequences at `-O2` without other flags:

- Compensated (Kahan) summation is simplified away: a single-precision Kahan sum of 10^7 terms 0.1 had a relative
  error of 1.1e-2 at `-O2` (the same with `-fp-model fast=2`) and 1.5e-8 with `-O2 -fp-model precise` or at
  `-O0`.
- `ieee_is_nan(x)` and `x /= x` were still true for a NaN at the default model and with `-fp-model precise`;
  with `-fp-model fast=2` both were false.

Use `-fp-model precise` (or `strict`, which also gives access to the floating-point environment) for code whose
accuracy depends on the order of operations: compensated sums, error-free transformations, interval
arithmetic, reproducibility tests. `fobis assess` uses `-fp-model precise` and `-fp-model fast=2` among its
`rounding` variants for this family.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Floating-point contraction (FMA)
chunks.text:
The default target of ifx has no FMA instructions: `a*b + c` was not contracted at `-O2` (measured).
`-xHost` on an FMA processor, or `-march=x86-64-v3`, contracted it (`a*b = 1 - 2**-60`, `c = -1` gave
`-2**-60` instead of 0); `-no-fma` and `-fp-model precise` prevented the contraction in the same measurement.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Automatic arrays, temporaries and the stack
chunks.text:
ifx places automatic arrays and the temporary copies of array expressions on the stack. Measured, with an
8 MB stack limit: an automatic array of 4 million double-precision values and an overlapping section assignment
`a(2:n) = a(1:n-1) + a(2:n)` with n = 4 million both died at `-O2` with

```
forrtl: severe (174): SIGSEGV, segmentation fault occurred
```

and ran with `-heap-arrays`, which puts them on the heap. gfortran and nvfortran ran both programs without
flags (measured), so this crash typically appears when a code that works with other compilers is first built
with ifx. With OpenMP the stacks of the other threads are sized by `OMP_STACKSIZE`.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Precision promotion flags
chunks.text:
Measured `kind()` of each declaration:

| Flags | real | double precision | real(real32) | real(real64) | real(8) |
|-------|------|------------------|--------------|--------------|---------|
| none | 4 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-real-size 64` | 8 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-real-size 64 -double-size 128` | 8 | 16 | 4 | 8 | 8 |

Only declarations without an explicit kind are promoted: a code that declares its kinds through a kind module
(`real(R8P)`, `real(real64)`) is not changed by these flags; promote it by changing the kind parameter.
`-integer-size 64` makes default integers 8 bytes (measured).

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Sanitizers
chunks.text:
ifx accepts `-fsanitize=address` (compile and link). Measured: it catches stack and global buffer overflows;
a heap overflow through an assumed-size dummy was missed. ifort does not support it: it prints
`warning #10006: ignoring unknown option '-fsanitize=address'` and builds without it, so a sanitized ifort
build runs unchecked. `fobis build --shadow sanitize` refuses ifort for this reason.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Module files
chunks.text:
ifx refuses `.mod` files written by another compiler:

```
error #7013: This module file was not generated by any release of this compiler.   [MPI_F08]
```

(measured with the `mpi_f08` module of an Open MPI built with gfortran). Libraries used through modules (MPI,
HDF5, NetCDF) need a build made with the Intel compiler; Intel MPI ships its own `mpi` and `mpi_f08` modules
(`include/mpi/` of the installation).

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Standard conformance
chunks.text:
`-stand f18` warns about non-standard code; `-warn stderrors` makes those warnings errors and `-warn errors`
all warnings. `fobis build --shadow strict` builds with `-stand f18 -warn stderrors -warn errors`.

chunks.heading: Intel Fortran (ifx, ifort) > Optimisation reports and profiling
chunks.text:
`-qopt-report=3` writes the optimisation report to `.optrpt` files (FoBiS does not parse them). `-p`
instruments for gprof (`fobis profile --tool gprof`). `-qopenmp` enables OpenMP.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran)
chunks.text:
Facts about nvfortran (the NVIDIA HPC SDK compiler, formerly PGI) that change what a program computes, how it
fails, or whether it builds. "Measured" means observed on small programs with nvfortran 26.1 on x86-64 Linux
(an Alder Lake class processor with FMA); option texts are those printed by `nvfortran -help`. FoBiS uses this
family for `compiler = nvfortran` and `compiler = pgi`.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Default optimisation and target
chunks.text:
Without an `-O` flag nvfortran optimises at level 1; with `-g` and no `-O` at level 0; `-O` alone means level 2
(measured from `nvfortran -dryrun`, which shows `-opt N` in the back-end command).

nvfortran compiles for the processor it runs on: `nvfortran --version` names the target (`-tp alderlake` on
the measured machine). Binaries built on a newer processor may not run on an older one: set the target with `-tp=` explicitly
(`-tp=px` for a generic x86-64 target) when the build and the compute nodes differ.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > FMA is on, even at -O0
chunks.text:
Because the default target has FMA, nvfortran contracts `a*b + c` into a fused multiply-add at every
optimisation level. Measured: `a*b = 1 - 2**-60`, `c = -1` gave `-2**-60` (contracted) at `-O0`, at the default
level, at `-O2`, with `-fast` and with `-Kieee`; it gave 0 with `-Mnofma` or `-tp=px`. `-Kieee` does not
disable contraction. When nvfortran results differ from another compiler's in the last bits, build both with
contraction off (`-Mnofma` here, `-ffp-contract=off` for gfortran) to see whether FMA explains it.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > -fast
chunks.text:
`nvfortran -help -fast`: "Common optimizations; includes -O2 -Munroll=c:1 -Mlre -Mautoinline. Implies
-Mvect=simd -Mflushz -Mcache_align". `-Mflushz` flushes subnormal results to zero. Measured: a single-precision
Kahan sum kept its accuracy with `-fast` (relative error 1.5e-8, as at `-O2`), and `ieee_is_nan` still detected a
NaN.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Runtime checks
chunks.text:
`-Mbounds` checks array subscripts (measured, `-O0 -g -Mbounds -traceback`):

```
0: Subscript out of range for array a (kernels.f90: 18)
    subscript=11, lower bound=1, upper bound=10, dimension=1
```

`-Mchkptr` checks for null pointers; `-traceback` adds a call stack to runtime errors. `-Ktrap=fp` traps
invalid operations, division by zero and overflow: the measured division by zero ended with SIGFPE and no
message on stderr, so the location must come from a debugger.

`-Minit-real=snan` does not give a trap on uninitialised reals: measured, it writes the quiet NaN `7FC00000`,
so the program runs on with NaN instead of stopping at the first use. Compare its results with a gfortran or
ifx build under their checks to locate an uninitialised real.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > No sanitizer
chunks.text:
nvfortran 26.1 rejects `-fsanitize=address` with `nvfortran-Error-Unknown switch: -fsanitize=address`.
Memory errors in host code are found with a gfortran or ifx sanitized build of the same sources, or with
Valgrind; device memory errors with NVIDIA's `compute-sanitizer`.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Precision promotion flags
chunks.text:
Measured `kind()` of each declaration:

| Flags | real | double precision | real(real32) | real(real64) | real(8) |
|-------|------|------------------|--------------|--------------|---------|
| none | 4 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| `-r8` | 8 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |

`-r8` promotes only default `real`; explicit kinds are unchanged. `-i8` makes default integers 8 bytes
(measured).

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Module files
chunks.text:
nvfortran refuses `.mod` files written by another compiler:

```
NVFORTRAN-F-0004-Corrupt or Old Module file /opt/openmpi/.../lib/mpi_f08.mod (pm.f90: 3)
```

(measured with an Open MPI built with gfortran). The HPC SDK ships an Open MPI (HPC-X) built for nvfortran under
`comm_libs/`; use its `mpifort` or its modules.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Compiler messages
chunks.text:
Errors are reported as `NVFORTRAN-S-NNNN-message (file: line)` (severity letters: I information, W warning,
S severe, F fatal). `-Minfo=accel,mp,vect` reports what the compiler did with OpenACC and OpenMP regions and
loops, procedure by procedure (implicit data copies, loops run sequentially on the device, vectorised loops);
`fobis lint --compiler-feedback LOG` and `fobis bench --feedback` read these messages.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > GPU options
chunks.text:
`-acc` enables OpenACC, `-mp=gpu` OpenMP target offload, `-cuda` CUDA Fortran. `-gpu=cc80` selects the compute
capability (8.0 here; `ccnative`: the visible GPUs). `-gpu=mem:managed` puts allocatable data in CUDA managed memory,
which hides missing data clauses: a code that is correct only with managed memory can fail with
`-gpu=mem:separate`. Device code uses FMA unless `-gpu=nofma`.

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Standard conformance and profiling
chunks.text:
`-Mstandard` warns about non-standard code; with `-Werror` the warnings are errors
(`fobis build --shadow strict`). `-pg` instruments for gprof (`fobis profile --tool gprof`).

chunks.heading: NVIDIA Fortran (nvfortran) > Known bug: CUDA error 719 on a reduction into a declare-create variable
chunks.text:
An OpenACC `reduction` into a module variable declared with `!$acc declare create` has failed at run time with
CUDA error 719 (launch failure); documented with a reproducer in the hpc-practice pack, which
`fobis run --explain` cites when it recognises the error.
